artboards.title: Direction A — four steps, side by side
Direction B — a rail, one step open
Where your own work is kept

annotations.text:
The one rule that fixes the origin problem:

Anything YOU own is purple on a purple wash — hooks, replaced nodes, replaced template sections. Anything that ships with Companion is plain surface. Nothing else in the panel uses that hue, so "what did we change here" is answerable from across the room.

The warm brand yellow stays out of the editor on purpose; the panel borrows the theme's own hues so it works in light, dark and high contrast.

Hooks got the arrow you asked for.

A before-hook sits above its node with the arrow pointing DOWN into it. An after-hook sits below with the arrow coming UP out of it. Several hooks at one anchor share a single connector, so three hooks is one line, not three.

auto is out of the flow.

It is a band above the four steps that says what it is in a sentence — not a fifth column pretending to be a peer.

classify-size IS a node — it just cannot move.

A node with a grab handle is free to reorder. A node with a padlock is held by something that reads it. The node detail names what is holding it, in a sentence.

80 hover buttons become 16.

One "Attach" per phase. The anchor and the side become a choice inside the flow — where there is room to say what each one means — instead of a target you have to hit.

What I would cut:

· The per-node + before / + after buttons (80 of them).
· The kind abbreviations INVST / AUTHR / GATE / CTRL — an icon on the card, the full word in the detail.
· reads: on the card. It only matters when you try to move something, and then the padlock says so.
· The per-step "produces X" footer — the file already sits on the node that writes it.
· Opening the raw .md as the default click. Read it in the panel; "Open the file" stays for when you want the editor.

When the panel is narrow:

Four columns become Direction B — the rail stays, one step opens below it. The rail is the thing you must never lose, so it is the thing that survives every width.
